# incast <a href="https://accidda.github.io/incast/"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="incast website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

`incast` is an R package for infectious disease nowcasting and forecasting developed as part of **[Insight Net](https://www.cdc.gov/insight-net)**, a **[CDC Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics](https://www.cdc.gov/forecast-outbreak-analytics/index.html)** initiative. It provides a unified framework for generating, evaluating, and operationalising infectious disease forecasts.

It fetches (`get_data()`) and validates input data (`check_data()`), optionally applies nowcasting to adjust for reporting delays (`get_ncast()`), evaluates models by cross-validation (`get_cv()`), and generates forecasts (`get_fcast()`).

## Installation

You can install the development version of incast from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ACCIDDA/incast")
```

## Quick start
```{r example-data, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE}
library(incast)
tail(example_data)
```

```{r forecast, eval = TRUE}
fcast <- example_data |>
  check_data() |>
  get_ncast() |>
  get_cv(eval_start_date = as.Date("2024-10-01")) |>
  get_fcast()

fcast

fcast |> autoplot()
```

Save and upload to [myRespiLens](https://www.respilens.com/myrespilens):
```{r respilens, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
fcast$hub$model_out_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    location = dplyr::recode(
      location,
      CA = "06",
      NY = "36"
    )
  ) |>
  write.csv("myrespilens_forecast.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Citation

If you use `incast` in your work, please cite the package as follows:
```{r citation}
citation("incast")
```

## Acknowledgements

The package relies on the [`baselinenowcast`](https://baselinenowcast.epinowcast.org/) and [`fable`](https://fable.tidyverts.org/) framework for time series nowcasting and forecasting. It produces forecasts in the [`hubverse`](https://hubverse.io/) format for submission to the [CDC Forecast Hubs](https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-modeling-and-forecasting/about/index.html).
